column1: # agent-comms credential environment table — THE one place to extend what a bound review leg's
# child environment is stripped of, and how each built-in adapter selects its authentication route.
# Read only by helpers/access_profiles.py, from the file installed beside it. There is deliberately
# no environment override: a second table beside the one the docs name is how a scrub goes stale.
# A bound leg (`panel dispatch --bindings`) gets a credential-scrubbed environment. The scrub set is the
# UNION of three sources, never one alone: every credential name in configuration (access.json, every
# agents.json `credentials` mapping and `connection.api_key_env`), the name patterns hard-coded in
# below. Only the leg's OWN credential is restored afterwards, under the name its adapter consumes.
#   scrub         <NAME>      one environment variable that selects a credential or an endpoint but
#                             matches no pattern (a cloud route switch, a base URL override)
#   scrub-prefix  <PREFIX>    every environment variable starting with this prefix
#                 how <adapter> is made to use exactly the bound billing route. `adapter` is a built-in
#                 provider name (codex) or `opencode` for a custom profile. `supported` means
#                 the route selection is explicit AND can be read back from what the launcher wrote;
#                 `unsupported` means it is not, and a leg bound to that pair is REFUSED
#                 (auth-route-unsupported) rather than run on the hope that an environment key wins
#                 over a saved login. The consumed variable is the name the adapter reads its API key
#                 from (`-` = none: a login, or the profile's own credentials mapping). Login files
#                 are relative to the adapter's home (codex: $CODEX_HOME).
# Evidence for the auth rows (2026-10-03, local and read-only; no live provider call was made):
# - gemini: no auth rows. The provider now runs through the Antigravity CLI directly, in the operator's own
#   home, so there is no isolated login to bind and no route selection a launcher can write and read back
#   (a bound leg is refused `gemini-unsupported`). The `scrub` rows below still apply to any bound leg.
# - codex subscription: the leg runs on the auth.json staged into its isolated CODEX_HOME. The staged
#   file's own `auth_mode` field is read back; every API-key variable is scrubbed, so nothing else can
# - codex api: codex-cli 0.160.0 carries a `forced_login_method` config key and a CODEX_API_KEY
#   variable (strings in the installed binary), but nothing here shows the ACP adapter honours either
#   for a mounted turn, and a live trial needs separate authorization. So the pair stays unsupported:
#   a codex leg bound to billing `api` is refused until that is established and this row is changed.
# - opencode (a custom profile): its isolated runtime has no login of its own; the profile's
#   `credentials` mapping is the only authentication it has.
